name: Hopkinton
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Hopkinton, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Hopkinton, MA: the Holiday Stroll with free carriage and train rides, Santa's fire truck tree lighting, and calm Santa visits.
lede: Hopkinton spends one December Saturday on its Town Common, with carriage rides, a Girl Scout tree lighting and Santa rolling in for the big moment, and local groups add quieter Santa visits around it.
celebrates: The Hopkinton Chamber of Commerce runs the Holiday Stroll each December, when local businesses open their doors and families collect passport stamps for a chance at a cash prize. The Hopkinton Center for the Arts holds a holiday marketplace, horse-drawn carriages circle the Town Common, and an ice sculpture goes up nearby. The day builds toward Santa's arrival and the Girl Scouts' holiday tree lighting, with caroling on the Common. The holiday lights around the Common came back after a community fundraising effort, and in 2026 the town approved a $25,000 purchase of new lights. The Hopkinton Lions Club also hosts a free, semi-private Santa visit for children with special needs.
lastyear: In 2025 the Holiday Stroll took place on Saturday, December 6, from 10 am to 3 pm, with 26 Hopkinton businesses on the passport list and a $300 cash prize for completed passports. The Hopkinton Center for the Arts ran its marketplace and festival of light program, and there were carriage rides and an ice sculpture demonstration on the Common. The John Warren Masonic Lodge offered free child ID kits, and Santa read The Night Before Christmas there at noon and 2 pm. Santa then arrived at the Common by horse-drawn carriage for the tree lighting.
facts: Hopkinton was incorporated in 1715, and it has been the starting line of the Boston Marathon since 1924, when the course was lengthened to the Olympic distance and the start moved west from Ashland. In 1966 Roberta Gibb jumped into the race from the bushes in Hopkinton and became the first woman to run Boston. The 2026 Holiday Stroll moves later in the day so it ends with the Girl Scouts' tree lighting, and it adds a trackless train with a Polar Express theme.
trains: Hopkinton has no Commuter Rail station of its own, but the MBTA Framingham/Worcester Line stops in neighboring Ashland and Southborough, with trains to Back Bay and South Station in Boston. The MBTA's family travel site notes that kids 11 and under ride the Commuter Rail for free, which makes a family trip into Boston for the holidays cheaper. For a holiday train through Christmas lights, Edaville in Carver runs its seasonal festival, and the 2026 Hopkinton Stroll has its own trackless Polar Express train.

kidfact: Every April, about 30,000 runners line up in Hopkinton to start the Boston Marathon. In December, the same small town center fills up with families waiting for Santa instead.
faq: When is the Hopkinton Holiday Stroll?

The Hopkinton Chamber of Commerce holds the Holiday Stroll on a Saturday in early December. In 2025 it ran from 10 am to 3 pm on December 6. Each year it brings business open houses, a passport challenge with a cash prize, carriage rides and a holiday marketplace run by the Hopkinton Center for the Arts, and it ends with Santa and the tree lighting.
Where is the Hopkinton tree lighting?

The holiday tree lighting happens on the Hopkinton Town Common on Main Street, in the center of town. The Girl Scouts host the lighting at the end of the Holiday Stroll, with caroling on the Common, and Santa arrives just before the lights go on. Holiday lights also go up around the Common for the season.
Is there a sensory-friendly Santa in Hopkinton?

Yes. The Hopkinton Lions Club runs Santa's Special Kids, a free, semi-private meet and greet for children with special or mental health needs. Families register ahead of time, and each child gets a gift bag and a photo with Santa, with cookies and hot chocolate in a calmer setting than a busy store line.
Can you take the train to Hopkinton for Christmas events?

Hopkinton has no Commuter Rail station. The nearest stops are Ashland and Southborough on the MBTA Framingham/Worcester Line, a short drive from the Town Common. Families going into Boston for holiday sights can ride from either station, and the MBTA says kids 11 and under ride the Commuter Rail for free.
